drhp.business: We are a consumer-focused, digital only, credit-led financial services platform for Middle India customers providing access to full suite of financial products through a network of Financial Partners, including our NBFC subsidiary, on our Moneyview mobile application. Our promise to our users is to offer personalized financial products with responsible and transparent terms, delivered via a convenient and user-friendly digital experience. “Registered Users” refers to the cumulative number of users who have accessed our website or mobile application through a unique mobile number or email …
drhp.one_liner: Through integrations with 48 Financial Partners as of June 30, 2026, including our NBFC subsidiary, WFPL, we offer a suite of financial products tailored to the evolving needs of Middle India.
risks: Our Company acts as a lending service provider (“LSP”) for our personal loan product, facilitating loan origination and end-to-end servicing by providing support for onboarding, credit evaluation, collections, and customer servicing.

Gross Stage 3 loans are defined as Total Gross Loans which are more than 90 days past due (“DPD”) from their contractual payments of principal and/or interest and all other loans of such customer as at the last day of the relevant period/Fiscal, and include loans which continue to be classified as Gross Stage 3 Loans till all overdues are cleared, as prescribed by relevant RBI guidelines.

While our mobile application had a 4.8-star rating on a mobile application store as of June 30, 2026, reflecting strong user satisfaction, we have also received negative customer reviews on some platforms, which could individually or cumulatively impact our brand value and reputation.

Our brand and reputation may be affected by various factors, including our failure to satisfy user expectations regarding the quality or reliability of our products, data protection and privacy concerns, negative perceptions regarding our compliance functions and regulatory adherence, any regulatory action, litigation and government investigations against us, as well as any operational failures or service disruptions.

While we receive customer complaints in the ordinary course of business, such complaints have not had any material adverse impact on our business and operations in the three month periods ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
We operate a digital lending platform and act as an LSP under the DL Directions, which also govern how we interact with borrowers, disclose loan terms, handle data, and manage customer grievances.
WFPL must comply with the prescribed requirements, including classification of NPAs and provisioning, Know your customer (“KYC”) requirements, and other internal control mechanisms.

In the past, the RBI has made certain observations and sought clarifications regarding WFPL’s operations, including delays in submission of certain forms and returns in the relevant portal, mismatches in total liabilities in its balance sheet for Fiscals 2023 and 2022 and backlog of customers’ KYC data to be updated with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest as of a certain date, to which WFPL has duly responded.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Executive Summary • India’s nominal Gross Domestic Product (“GDP”) is projected to grow at ~9.5% Compound Annual Growth Rate (“CAGR”) between FY2026 and FY2031P, anchored by rising private consumption enabled by the growth in household credit • This economic growth is supported by favourable macroeconomic tailwinds, including a young workforce, rapid urbanisation, rising household incomes, and deepening digital penetration.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: This expansion is likely to be led by Middle India, with data-led digital credit products - leveraging alternative data for underwriting and risk assessment - emerging as a key engine of retail loan growth. • India’s retail lending market is thus set to nearly double by FY2031P, with retail loan sanctions projected to grow at a CAGR of 13-15% from ₹76.6 trillion (~US$0.9 trillion) in FY2026 to ₹138-151 trillion (US$1.5-1.7 trillion) by FY2031P.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Within this, unsecured loans have emerged as the faster-growing segment, expected to grow at a CAGR of 17-19% between FY2026 and FY2031P. a.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Personal loans, in particular, grew at a CAGR of ~43% between FY2021 and FY2026 and are projected to reach ₹33-36 trillion (US$0.37-0.40 trillion) by FY2031P, expanding at a CAGR of 18-20% over FY2026-FY2031P. b.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Digital personal loans accounted for ~15% of unsecured personal loans sanctioned in FY2026 and represent the fastest-growing segment within unsecured lending, projected to grow at a CAGR of 26-27% over FY2026-FY2031P.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The expansion and improved accessibility of formal credit have underpinned economic growth and strengthened private consumption by enabling households to meet a broader array of essential and aspirational needs. 1.2.1 India’s private consumption is growing faster than GDP, providing an additional impetus to overall economic growth India’s private consumption continues to grow at a pace exceeding overall GDP growth, with PFCE registering a robust ~13% CAGR between FY2021 and FY2026.

other_material_facts.value: With strong underlying growth in consumption spending, discretionary household expenditures in India are projected to further expand, reaching 59% by FY2031P. _enrichment_conflicts.deterministic_value: Through integrations with 48 Financial Partners as of June 30, 2026, including our NBFC subsidiary, WFPL, we offer a suite of financial products tailored to the evolving needs of Middle India.

We are a consumer-focused, digital only, credit-led financial services platform for Middle India customers providing access to full suite of financial products through a network of Financial Partners, including our NBFC subsidiary, on our Moneyview mobile application. Our promise to our users is to offer personalized financial products with responsible and transparent terms, delivered via a convenient and user-friendly digital experience. “Registered Users” refers to the cumulative number of users who have accessed our website or mobile application through a unique mobile number or email address at least once since inception through the last date of the relevant period/Fiscal.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our Company acts as a lending service provider (“LSP”) for our personal loan product, facilitating loan origination and end-to-end servicing by providing support for onboarding, credit evaluation, collections, and customer servicing.
- Gross Stage 3 loans are defined as Total Gross Loans which are more than 90 days past due (“DPD”) from their contractual payments of principal and/or interest and all other loans of such customer as at the last day of the relevant period/Fiscal, and include loans which continue to be classified as Gross Stage 3 Loans till all overdues are cleared, as prescribed by relevant RBI guidelines.
- While our mobile application had a 4.8-star rating on a mobile application store as of June 30, 2026, reflecting strong user satisfaction, we have also received negative customer reviews on some platforms, which could individually or cumulatively impact our brand value and reputation.
- Our brand and reputation may be affected by various factors, including our failure to satisfy user expectations regarding the quality or reliability of our products, data protection and privacy concerns, negative perceptions regarding our compliance functions and regulatory adherence, any regulatory action, litigation and government investigations against us, as well as any operational failures or service disruptions.
- While we receive customer complaints in the ordinary course of business, such complaints have not had any material adverse impact on our business and operations in the three month periods ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, and Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
- We operate a digital lending platform and act as an LSP under the DL Directions, which also govern how we interact with borrowers, disclose loan terms, handle data, and manage customer grievances.
- WFPL must comply with the prescribed requirements, including classification of NPAs and provisioning, Know your customer (“KYC”) requirements, and other internal control mechanisms.
- In the past, the RBI has made certain observations and sought clarifications regarding WFPL’s operations, including delays in submission of certain forms and returns in the relevant portal, mismatches in total liabilities in its balance sheet for Fiscals 2023 and 2022 and backlog of customers’ KYC data to be updated with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest as of a certain date, to which WFPL has duly responded.
